provenance.method: passive sniffer + active send-and-capture + echo-verified CameraSession
provenance.notes: 3/3 start/stop cycles echo-verified on real hardware via examples/record_start_stop.py. echo_operation is the operation byte the camera itself uses when reporting this category/parameter (distinct from ASSIGN used by the controller's command). Echo payload trailing bytes 00 40 00 01 03 not yet understood — hypothesis: SDI Cat 10 Param 1 transport-mode struct, see docs/protocol.md. 2026-07-09: data_type relabelled BOOL -> INT8 when DataType was remapped to the official spec coding; the captured wire byte (0x01) is unchanged.

provenance.method: external reverse-engineering document (CODEC_RES_FPS_6K_G2.docx, 2026-07-20) — byte layout and codec/variant id tables transcribed; report side re-confirmed by this repo's passive capture (sniffer_settings.py, 2026-07-20); write side not yet sent by this repo's tooling
provenance.notes: Payload is two int8 elements [codec_id, variant_id] from the top-level `codecs` table (10-byte packet, e.g. FF 06 00 00 0A 00 01 00 03 03 for BRAW 5:1). Matches the official spec's 10.0 Codec parameter coordinates, but the observed data-type byte is 0x01 (INT8), not an array marker. Reserved byte 0x00 — differs from recording and video_format (0x01). OBSERVED LIMITATION: changes the quality variant within the active codec family but does NOT switch BRAW <-> ProRes even though it carries a codec id — codec-family switches require the video_format packet's dimension_enum. 2026-07-20 passive capture: camera-originated 0x0A/0x00 reports confirmed on the wire — operation 0x02, data-type byte 0x01, payload exactly 2 bytes; observed 02 00 (ProRes HQ), 03 02 (BRAW 3:1), 03 03 (BRAW 5:1), confirming both codec ids and those three variant ids. 2026-07-20 active send (send_settings_command.py --packet codec_quality --codec ProRes --variant HQ, TX FF 06 00 00 0A 00 01 00 02 00, camera on BRAW at the time): operator confirmed on real hardware the codec did NOT change — direct confirmation of the cross-family-write-is-a-no-op limitation above. The captured response window itself is NOT usable evidence: it shows no 0x0A/0x00 report at all, only unrelated post-connect initial-payload packets (recording status, reel/scene/take/camera-id metadata) — send_settings_command.py wrote immediately after connecting with no settle delay, racing the camera's initial burst (same hazard CameraSession.connect_settle_s exists for, docs/session_and_verification.md). Fixed same date via --connect-settle-seconds (default 6.0s); this run predates the fix. Still untested: a same-family variant-only write (e.g. BRAW Q0 -> BRAW 5:1) — status stays CANDIDATE pending a clean echo and that coverage; see docs/settings.md §6 for the full writeup.

provenance.method: external reverse-engineering document (CODEC_RES_FPS_6K_G2.docx, 2026-07-20) — byte layout, fps byte and dimension_enum tables transcribed; not yet re-verified by this repo's capture tooling
capture_refs: tools/captures/POCKET_6K_G2_v7.9/ — 16 files timestamped 20260720T1527xx through T1541xx, one per --dimension-enum probe (local, gitignored, see docs/settings.md §7 for the full list)
provenance.notes: The FORMAT packet: five int8 elements [fps_int, m_rate, dimension_enum, 0, 0] (13-byte packet, e.g. FF 09 00 01 01 00 01 00 19 00 08 00 00 for 25 fps 4K DCI/BRAW). dimension_enum encodes resolution AND codec family together (see `resolutions.*.dimension_enums`) — this is the packet that actually switches BRAW <-> ProRes; codec_quality alone does not. Parameter is 0x00 (spec 1.0 Video Mode int8 x5), NOT 0x09. The two trailing zero elements are unexplained — hypothesis: the spec's interlaced and colorspace video-mode elements. 2026-07-20 passive capture: NO report on 0x01/0x00 appeared in any window, INCLUDING body-initiated BRAW<->ProRes switches — the camera reports settings state via 0x01/0x09 and 0x0A/0x00 instead. 2026-07-20 active send (pre-connect-settle-fix): operator confirmed a switch to ProRes/UHD but the captured window was burst noise — see docs/settings.md §6. 2026-07-20 dimension_enum probe sweep (post-fix, send_settings_command.py --dimension-enum, 25fps, docs/settings.md §7): sent all of 0x01,0x02,0x03,0x04,0x05,0x06,0x07,0x08,0x09,0x0D,0x0F,0x10,0x11,0x12,0x13,0x14 and decoded a CLEAN echo for every one, on the 0x01/0x09 (recording_format) coordinates plus a 0x0A/0x00 codec-family report — 0x01/0x00 itself still never echoes, confirming the earlier hypothesis was right about where to look. The 8 enums already in `resolutions.*.dimension_enums` (0x03,0x06,0x08,0x0D,0x0F,0x12,0x13,0x14) each produced an exact width/height/codec-family match, operator-confirmed and echo-confirmed together — the strongest evidence any settings family has. 0x01,0x02,0x04,0x05,0x07,0x09,0x11 all produced NO change (the 1/9 report simply reflected whatever resolution was already active) — recorded as known-invalid, not merely untried. 0x10 SPECIFICALLY REFUTES the earlier '3.7K Anamorphic alt' hypothesis: it also produced no change, so it is not a second enum for 3728x3104 — removed from `resolutions`. 0x0A/0x0B/0x0C and every value ≥ 0x15 remain untried. 4K DCI under ProRes STILL has no known enum — none of the tried values produced it; either its enum lies in the untried range or 4K DCI/ProRes isn't reachable via a single dimension_enum at all. Mechanistic insight: the camera issues a 0x01/0x09 status reflection after ANY video_format write, valid or not — it is not an error signal, just 'here is my current state.' Despite this being the strongest evidence yet, status stays CANDIDATE: this is the raw tool's echo, not CameraSession.set_video_format's own verification path — run examples/change_codec.py for that before promoting.

provenance.method: external reverse-engineering document (CODEC_RES_FPS_6K_G2.docx, 2026-07-20) — byte layout and fps/resolution encodings transcribed; report side re-confirmed by this repo's passive capture (sniffer_settings.py, 2026-07-20); write side not yet sent by this repo's tooling
provenance.notes: Five little-endian int16 elements [fps_int, sensor_fps_int, width, height, frame_flags] (18-byte packet, e.g. FF 0E 00 01 01 09 82 00 19 00 19 00 00 10 70 08 10 00 for 25 fps 4096x2160). data_type 0x82 (INT16_ARRAY) is the claimed WRITE byte — the camera's own 0x01/0x09 reports carry data-type byte 0x02 (plain INT16) instead, sniffer-confirmed 2026-07-20 along with the exact element order (e.g. 32 00 32 00 00 10 70 08 10 00 = 50fps 4096x2160 flags 0x0010; 3C 00 3C 00 00 18 00 0A 13 00 = 59.94 6144x2560 flags 0x0013). NEW from that capture: flags 0x0000 reported at 6K 3:2 (full sensor) — so 0x0010 is NOT a plain 'exact rate' marker; the three observed values (0x0000/0x0010/0x0013) decode exactly as the official 1.9 flags bitfield (bit0 file-M-rate, bit1 sensor-M-rate, bit4 windowed), making the windowed bit resolution-dependent. `fps_modes.frame_flags` still stores the values as transcribed (valid for windowed resolutions); writing 6K 3:2 may need 0x0000. 2026-07-20 active send (pre-connect-settle-fix): operator confirmed both resolution and fps changed, but the captured window was burst noise — see docs/settings.md §6. 2026-07-20 dimension_enum probe sweep (post-fix, docs/settings.md §7): the 6K 3:2 flags-0x0000 finding was INDEPENDENTLY RE-CONFIRMED at a different fps (25fps here vs 50fps in the first sighting) via a clean decoded 0x01/0x09 report — the windowed-bit hypothesis now has two independent confirmations. Status stays CANDIDATE pending a clean echo for a WRITE this repo's tooling actually sent with the 0x82 byte specifically (the probe sweep sent video_format writes, whose resulting state this family's own report happens to carry — see commands.video_format.provenance) and CameraSession round-trip confirmation. sensor_fps_int defaults to fps_int (off-speed unexplored).

codecs._comment: CANDIDATE — transcribed from CODEC_RES_FPS_6K_G2.docx; provenance rides with commands.codec_quality. Variant ids are per-codec. BRAW variant id 6 is unobserved (gap between 12:1 at 5 and Q1 at 7) — do not invent it.

resolutions._comment: provenance rides with commands.video_format / commands.recording_format. dimension_enums are keyed per codec because the enum locks resolution and codec family together. All 8 dimension_enums below are now CONFIRMED (2026-07-20 dimension_enum probe sweep, docs/settings.md §7): each was sent via send_settings_command.py --dimension-enum and produced a decoded 0x01/0x09 report whose width/height matches exactly, plus a 0x0A/0x00 codec-family report matching the listed codec — not just the original external-document transcription. 4K DCI is the only resolution offered under both codecs, but only its BRAW enum is known — the ProRes one was searched for across every untried value in 0x01-0x14 and NOT found (see commands.video_format.provenance); it may lie in the unexplored 0x0A-0x0C/>=0x15 range, or may not be reachable via a single dimension_enum at all. A previously-recorded second entry for 3728x3104 ('3.7K Anamorphic alt', enum 0x10) was REMOVED 2026-07-20: 0x10 was probed and produced no state change at all (not a valid resolution selector), refuting that hypothesis. 2026-07-20 captures also showed frame_flags 0x0000 reported at 6K 3:2 (both @ 50fps and @ 25fps, two independent sessions) vs 0x0010 at every other resolution — the 0x10 bit looks like the spec's resolution-dependent 'windowed' flag, see commands.recording_format.provenance.

fps_modes._comment: CANDIDATE — transcribed from CODEC_RES_FPS_6K_G2.docx; provenance rides with commands.video_format / commands.recording_format. fps_int is shared by both packet families; m_rate is video_format's flag (0 exact, 1 NTSC/drop); frame_flags is recording_format's int16 as transcribed (0x0010 'exact', 0x0013 'NTSC/drop'). CAVEAT (2026-07-20 capture): the 0x10 bit appears to be the spec's resolution-dependent 'windowed' flag, not part of the fps encoding — the camera reported 0x0000 at 6K 3:2; these values hold as-written for windowed resolutions only. See commands.recording_format.provenance.

provenance.method: passive observation from examples/record_start_stop.py real-hardware logs during induced SD card slow-write-speed testing
provenance.notes: Raw bytes FF 07 00 00 09 01 01 02 00 FE 00. Payload byte at offset 1 flips 0x01 (nominal) -> 0xFE (-2, low_margin) 0.1-1.4s before every autonomous unexpected stop observed on a known-slow SD card — 6/6 occurrences, 3 cycles x 2 camera models (POCKET_6K_G2 v7.9, POCKET_6K_PRO v8.6). Never -2 in 7 unrelated normal-session logs, where this notification fires once per session and stays 0x01. Payload offsets 0 and 2 are constant (0x00) in every sample, both conditions. NOT yet isolated from other possible autostop causes (card full, card removed, power loss) — 'slow write speed' is inference from test context, not read off the wire alone. CAVEAT ADDED 2026-07-20 (docs/settings.md §7's dimension_enum probe sweep): this same -2/low_margin reading appeared in essentially every one of that sweep's ~18 connect cycles over roughly 15 minutes, with no recording ever active — i.e. it can persist as a steady state for extended periods outside any recording context, not just as a brief pre-stop warning. This further weakens (does not disprove) a simple 'low_margin predicts an imminent autostop' reading — it may instead reflect a per-(card, resolution/bitrate) threshold that happens to sit below nominal for this SD card at the BRAW resolutions used in that sweep, unrelated to recording at all. See docs/recording.md's 'Camera-initiated stop detection' section.
